# A struct literal's omitted field reads its declared default, or its type's
# zero, on every language alike.
#
# The checker writes every field a literal leaves out, so nothing after it
# can tell an omitted field from a written one. Before, JavaScript wrote only
# the fields named, so an omitted one read undefined: `p.y + 1` was NaN and
# `p.c.r` threw. Go left an omitted enum field "", which no member is, so
# `p.tone == Tone.calm` was false on every Go target.

mkdir none html bubbletea android

cp app.sngl none/app.sngl
sngl test --platform=none none/app.sngl
stdout 'ok +4 tests, 0 failures'

cp app.sngl html/app.sngl
sngl test --platform=html html/app.sngl
stdout 'ok +4 tests, 0 failures'

cp app.sngl bubbletea/app.sngl
sngl test --platform=bubbletea bubbletea/app.sngl
stdout 'ok +4 tests, 0 failures'

cp app.sngl android/app.sngl
sngl test --platform=android android/app.sngl
stdout 'ok +4 tests, 0 failures'

-- app.sngl --
import test "sngl:test"
import ui "sngl:ui"

enum Tone { calm, loud }

struct Inner {
    n    int
    tone Tone
}

struct P {
    x     int
    y     int
    w     float = 1.5
    c     color
    tone  Tone
    inner Inner
    tags  list[string]
    maybe option[int]
}

var held P = {x=1}

func made() P {
    return {x=2}
}

func testHeld(t test.Test) {
    t.assert(held.y + 1 == 1)
    t.assert(held.w == 1.5)
    t.assert(held.c.r == 0)
    t.assert(held.tone == Tone.calm)
    t.assert(held.inner.n == 0)
    t.assert(held.inner.tone == Tone.calm)
    t.assert(held.tags.length() == 0)
    t.assert(held.maybe == null)
}

func testMade(t test.Test) {
    var p = made()
    t.assert(p.y == 0)
    t.assert(p.tone == Tone.calm)
    t.assert(p.inner.tone == Tone.calm)
    t.assert(p.inner == Inner{n=0, tone=Tone.calm})
}

func testSpread(t test.Test) {
    var p = P{...made(), y=3}
    t.assert(p.x == 2)
    t.assert(p.y == 3)
    t.assert(p.w == 1.5)
    t.assert(p.tone == Tone.calm)
}

func testZeroVar(t test.Test) {
    var p P
    t.assert(p.w == 1.5)
    t.assert(p.tone == Tone.calm)
    t.assert(p.inner.tone == Tone.calm)
}

ui.window {
    ui.text(value="{held.x}")
}
